class.name: WeatherSkyMaterial
class.brief_description: A physical sky with volumetric clouds from the weather map.
class.description: An atmosphere ([member atmosphere_model]) with clouds raymarched through it, after Guerrilla's Nubis and Frostbite: a layer on a round planet, Beer-Lambert steps that conserve energy, a forward and a back Henyey-Greenstein lobe, Wrenninge's multiple scattering octaves and a two-stream diffuse term, and six steps towards the sun from each sample. The clouds are drawn in the half resolution pass, with fewer steps for the radiance map that lights the scene. With [member cloud_reprojection], a sixteenth of the screen's pixels are marched a frame and the rest are kept from the frames before. A [WeatherMap3D] in the scene sends it the cloud cover, type, storms and drift at its [member WeatherMap3D.update_rate]; without one, the sky shows the defaults. Set the [Sky]'s [member Sky.process_mode] to [constant Sky.PROCESS_MODE_INCREMENTAL] or [constant Sky.PROCESS_MODE_REALTIME] so the lighting follows the moving clouds. Its uniforms are under [b]Shader Parameters[/b]: the older atmosphere's (as [PhysicalSkyMaterial]); the [code]atmosphere[/code] group ([code]atmo_steps[/code], [code]atmo_radiance_steps[/code], [code]atmo_cloud_air_steps[/code], [code]atmo_cloud_shadow_steps[/code] (steps through the air under the cloud tops, each reading the clouds' shadow, which draws shafts across the sky; 0 for none), and [code]atmo_far_water[/code], 1 when open sea runs on past the scene to the horizon); and [code]cloud_steps[/code], [code]cloud_radiance_steps[/code], [code]cloud_light_steps[/code], [code]cloud_far[/code] and [code]cloud_brightness[/code]. The [code]weather_map[/code] group is set by the map. Under path tracing, bounce rays see the clouds through the radiance map. Enable [member Environment.pathtracing_sky_shader_enabled] for camera rays to see them at full detail. Dusk and night skies are dark, smooth gradients that 8-bit output steps into bands: enable [member Viewport.use_debanding] (or [code]rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/use_debanding[/code]), which dithers after tonemapping. The sky adds no dither of its own, since noise added before exposure and tonemapping is scaled by them. [b]Note:[/b] The moon lights the air but is not drawn yet, and there are no stars yet.

method.name: set_atmosphere_lights
method.description: Lights the scattering atmosphere with two bodies above the air: directions toward them, and their irradiance in light energy units before the air. [SkyClock] calls this when [member SkyClock.drive_light_energy] is on. Until it is called, the sky takes the first directional light as the sun above the air.

method.name: set_moon_angular_size
method.description: The moon disc's angular diameter. [SkyClock] sets it from the moon's distance. The disc is shaded by Lommel-Seeliger from the sun's direction (so its phase and terminator follow the clock), with earthshine on its dark side, and sums to the moon's illuminance. The shader parameter [code]moon_disc_enabled[/code] (on) switches it.

method.name: set_aerosol
method.description: The weather's aerosol haze in the sky's air: [param extinction] at the ground (1/m; 0 for none), its single-scatter [param albedo], its scale [param height] (m), and the distance [param from] the camera along each view ray where it starts (the volumetric fog's reach, which draws the nearer part). It scatters with the sun's light through the clouds' shadow, so the shafts carry on past the volumetric fog, and dims the sun's disc and the stars. [WeatherMap3D] calls this from [member WeatherMap3D.aerosol_haze].

method.name: set_cloud_shadow_map
method.description: The clouds' shadow for the sky's air (its shafts): a [param map] baked in the sun's plane, red the sun's beam transmittance through the cloud deck and green its diffuse transmission, with the plane's world axes [param axis_u] and [param axis_v], the corner of its square in that plane and its [param size] (m). [WeatherMap3D] bakes and sets it (40 km wide). Without one the shader marches the clouds toward the sun itself, coarser.

method.name: set_star_sky
method.description: Places the stars (the Yale Bright Star Catalogue, about 9,100 stars, what the eye sees): [param celestial] turns the J2000 equator frame (x toward right ascension 0h, z toward the north celestial pole) into the world, and [param energy_per_lux] turns a star's illuminance above the air into light energy. [SkyClock] calls this with [method SkyClock.get_celestial_basis] when [member SkyClock.drive_light_energy] is on; until then no stars are drawn. The shader parameters [code]stars_enabled[/code] (on) and [code]star_brightness[/code] (1) switch and scale them.

members.member: The air's model. [constant ATMOSPHERE_SCATTERING] is Hillaire's (2020): Rayleigh, Mie and ozone marched per pixel over a transmittance table and a multiple scattering table baked once at start (about 0.3 s), lit by the sun and the moon, from the ground to space, through golden hour, twilight and the Earth's shadow. The clouds are seen through the air in front of them (aerial perspective) and reach the horizon. [constant ATMOSPHERE_PHYSICAL_SKY] is the older Preetham-based model of [PhysicalSkyMaterial], fitted to daylight, with clouds cut at [code]cloud_far[/code].

Temporal reprojection of the clouds, as Guerrilla's Nubis does: each frame one pixel of every 4x4 block is marched, in an order that covers all of them in 16 frames, and the rest are carried over from the frames before through the camera's turn (the sky shader's [code]half_res_reprojection[/code] render mode). The clouds come out at full resolution for a quarter of the half resolution pass's marching. Off, every half resolution pixel is marched every frame. Clouds that change fast trail by up to 16 frames.
